title: The garden loop's missing last step
question: The ringed cell is a pip an ant just carried home. It goes pale-tan, then vanishes 5 frames later, eaten -- does that read as the reason no pip has ever grown into a plant?
context_md:
Round 28, the fruit -> animal -> nest -> seedling loop (`Reports/lanes/evolution-lab-garden-loop.md`). Measured over 3 seeds x 120,000 frames on the played bed: `plants_from_pip` is **0 in every seed**, and this is the *only* seed where a pip survived long enough to be delivered at all (6 of 6 delivered pips were eaten; the other two seeds' bites never survived the gut roll, so no pip existed to test).

This sequence is seed 2, world frames 55,925-55,945: an ant carries a pip home, sets it down at (342,154) frame 55,932 (ringed), it settles two rows down as a `Powder` falls, and by frame 55,937 the cell reads empty again -- a second ant bit it. No pip in any of the three seeds has ever reached even its first scheduled germination check.

The upstream cause measured separately: standing windfall (fallen fruit) sits in columns the colony's own foot traffic never reaches on 67-100% of column-stops across the three seeds -- the fruiting understory (scramblers) stands outside the band the colony forages and founds in, which `played_bed.ron`'s own comments say was a deliberate, separately-measured trade for founder count. Full tables in the lane note.
